display: Kitchen-garden coordinator at a Brunswick primary school in Melbourne, running a weekly garden-and-cooking program for the whole school.

signals.text: I need a ute and a driver to collect about 20 hardwood sleepers from a sawmill in Thomastown.
The raised beds in the school garden have rotted out. Four won't survive spring and two are held together by luck, so we have six usable beds for 320 kids.
The grant I applied for to rebuild the beds fell through in August, and spring planting with the kids starts in October.
I'm after a handful of people with basic building skills for a Saturday build weekend. Plenty of people say 'I'm not a carpenter, mate', and I need the ones who'll turn up anyway.
I can't use treated pine near edible plants, so I need untreated hardwood or other food-safe timber offcuts.
The Bunnings community fund takes six weeks to apply for. I'd like a quicker route to small bits of funding or in-kind help.
The school's council-registered commercial kitchen sits empty every weekend, and I'd love to see it used by someone who needs it.
I don't know how to set up community use of a school facility (agreement, insurance, who's allowed), and I haven't had time to chase it up.
Only about 8 of my 25 parent volunteers are reliable, and getting people to commit is the hardest part of my job.
I'm stretched thin. Half my job is gardening with kids and the other half is begging for donations.
I'm learning permaculture on Thursday nights and would like to compare notes with people who run school or community gardens.
I'm training a rescue greyhound and would welcome tips from anyone who has done it.
My teenager wants to leave school for a trade apprenticeship. I'd value hearing from tradespeople or parents who've been through it.

offers.text: I run a kitchen-garden program where every class does a garden session and a cooking session each week, for about 320 students with 12 teachers as regular partners.
I can teach eight-year-olds to garden, and I know how to make planting, compost and chooks work with big groups of children.
The school has about 400 square metres of garden with a chook run, a compost bay and six fruit trees. I can host a visit or a skills-share there.

The school has a council-registered commercial kitchen with stainless benches, a big oven and six burners, and it's empty on weekends. The principal is open to community use under an agreement and insurance.
I have a roster of about 25 parent volunteers, 8 of them reliable, and can offer a ready group for community projects.
I have local business connections: the Brunswick Bunnings, a Coburg nursery, and two cafes that give us coffee grounds. I can introduce people who want to partner with a school.
I can give surplus veggies, seedlings and fruit from the garden in season, and I've promised Gus the sawmill man some in summer.
I'm working through a part-time permaculture course, including site analysis and soil biology, and can help others plan a small edible garden.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I run a small home catering business and my kitchen is too small to scale. Do you know of any licensed commercial kitchen I could hire on weekends?
catchers.can: I can raise it again with the principal, who is open to community use as long as there is an agreement and insurance. I can't promise anything, but I can tell you what the school would need from you.
catchers.confirm: Do you hold your own public liability insurance, or could you get it, and would you only need the kitchen outside school hours?

catchers.hypo: I'm a tradie with a ute and a free Saturday. Anything a school garden needs moved or built?
catchers.can: I need someone to collect about 20 hardwood sleepers from a Thomastown sawmill and bring them to Brunswick. If you can also help build raised beds on a Saturday, that's even better.
catchers.confirm: Can you drive a ute or trailer to Thomastown and Brunswick on a weekend, and are you happy to work alongside parents and kids' supervisors?

catchers.hypo: My company has leftover untreated timber, sleepers or off-cuts. Could a community garden use them?
catchers.can: I can use untreated hardwood or food-safe timber for raised garden beds. Treated pine is no use because it can't go near edible plants, so I'd ask about the timber first.
catchers.confirm: Is the timber untreated, or certified safe for use around food crops (not CCA, ACQ or other treated pine)?

catchers.hypo: I run a small local foundation, and our grant round was oversubscribed. Is there any smaller or in-kind help we could point a school towards?
catchers.can: I'm rebuilding the school's garden beds before spring planting with the kids, and a small grant or in-kind contribution would help right now. The school's P&C is also discussing funding.
catchers.confirm: Could you commit a small amount (under a few thousand dollars) or in-kind materials within a few weeks, not at the next full round?

catchers.hypo: Mei here. My husband is handy and we're free next Saturday. What should we bring?
catchers.can: Mei is one of my most reliable parent volunteers. I'd happily put her and her husband on the build weekend, and they could bring other families along.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to commit to a specific Saturday and help with basic building, such as drilling, lifting and screwing, not only supervising the kids?

catchers.hypo: My 15-year-old wants to leave school at the end of Year 10 to become an electrician. How do I support that without pushing him either way?
catchers.can: I'm living this too, with a teenager who's just done a week of work experience with a sparky. I can compare notes as a parent, and through my son I may be able to connect you with how he's finding the trade route.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for a parent-to-parent chat about a teen leaving school early for a trade, and not for formal career or legal advice?

catchers.hypo: I'm starting a school or community garden in my area. Where do I even begin with volunteers and donations?
catchers.can: I can share what has worked for me in recruiting volunteers, asking local businesses for donations, and running garden and cooking sessions for hundreds of kids.
catchers.confirm: Are you starting a garden program for a school or similar community group, and not a commercial farm or business?

catchers.hypo: I teach permaculture or run a community garden. Would a school like to host a workshop or an excursion?
catchers.can: I can host a small group at the school garden and fit it around lessons. Any visit needs the principal's approval and has to fit the school's insurance.
catchers.confirm: Are you offering a short, free or low-cost session suitable for primary-school children or parents, and can you share your insurance or working-with-children details?

forbids.text: I won't use treated timber anywhere near edible plants.
I can't hand over use of the school facilities without a proper agreement and insurance; the school's insurance limits who can use them.
I only work Monday to Thursday, part-time.
I have a budget of about $2,000 a term, so I can't pay for large purchases or services.
I won't share details about the school's internal politics or staff pay.
I won't put children's names, photos or personal details into any outside conversation.

projects.name: Rebuild the school garden beds
projects.text: Replace twelve rotting raised beds with hardwood ones before spring planting, using donated sleepers and a volunteer build weekend.

projects.name: Weekend community use of the school kitchen
projects.text: Open the school's council-registered commercial kitchen on weekends to a community cook, caterer or food group, under a proper agreement and insurance.
roles_needed: community cook or small food business
someone who has set up a school facility-hire agreement

policy.t1: The garden program and volunteer roster, the greyhound, and that the school's commercial kitchen sits empty every weekend and the principal is open to community use. Also what I need for a build weekend, such as a ute, handy volunteers and untreated hardwood.
policy.t2: That the garden's raised beds have rotted out, the grant fell through, spring planting with the kids starts in October, and I'm looking for funding or in-kind help. Also family matters, such as my teenager's apprenticeship plans, but only when a collaboration looks solid.
policy.never: Salary, school politics, children's personal details, and how much of the program rests on me.
